summary: Your report is readable and balanced, with a clear Not Ship conclusion and relevant cases. Strengths include stakeholder identification and structured for/against discussion. Key improvements: add the missing abstract, correct the 1% arithmetic and Volkswagen case details, align the recommendation with your conclusion, expand and format references, and include a visual element. These changes will raise evidence and structure marks.
next_steps: Add an abstract and revise Recommendation 1 so it clearly supports your Not Ship conclusion; specify the conditions under which Rachel should not ship.

Correct the arithmetic (1% of 5,000 = 50, not 500) and the Volkswagen case description (defeat devices concerned diesel emissions, not electric vehicles or crash tests); add more reputable references and format them consistently.
Include at least one visual element (e.g., a stakeholder/risk table) and proofread for typos; ensure all references have complete URLs and details.

criteria.C1: Excellent: You identify several ethical issues, link them to engineering design, and discuss competitive organisational context. You list stakeholders including Rachel, company, chip supplier, health department, and end-users. To sustain this top level, keep stakeholder interests integrated throughout the report, not only in the introduction.
criteria.C2: Very good: Your balanced section presents for and against arguments and reaches a clear Not Ship conclusion. To reach Excellent, deepen the objective arguments and provide decision-making recommendations for several different stakeholders, not just Rachel. Avoid speculative claims and tie each argument to stakeholder consequences.
criteria.C3: Very good: Your report is logically ordered from dilemma to for/against to ethical path and conclusion, and evidence supports Not Ship. However, the recommendation contradicts this conclusion. To reach Excellent, align the recommendation with your conclusion and demonstrate systematic understanding of ethical issues for all stakeholders throughout.
criteria.C4: Good: You use external cases and a code of ethics, but only four references, incomplete formatting, an arithmetic error (1% of 5,000 = 50, not 500), and a misstated Volkswagen case weaken evidence. To reach Very good, correct these errors, add adequate references, and include both qualitative and quantitative evidence accurately.
criteria.C5: Satisfactory: Sections are present except the required abstract; there are no figures or tables, some typos, and inconsistent references (e.g., malformed CNBC URL, missing BBC URL). To reach Good, add an abstract, include at least limited visual elements, proofread for language errors, and format references consistently and relevantly.
